claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my one child. His name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! Nice to meet you. Let's go through a few questions to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

First, could you tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex is 19, there are some specific conditions that need to be met for you to be eligible for Child Benefit.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training? This would include things like:
- A-levels or equivalent
- Scottish Highers
- NVQs up to Level 3
- A traineeship in England

(This does not include higher education such as university degrees or employment-based training like apprenticeships.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's in sixth form studying for his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is 19 and studying for his A-levels, he may still qualify.

Could you tell me when Alex turned 19? Specifically, was it before or after 31 August of this year?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He turned 19 before the 31st of August this year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex turned 19 before 31 August this year, there's one more important detail I need to clarify.

When did Alex start or enrol in his current A-level course? Specifically, did he start this course before he turned 19?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he started the A-level course before he turned 19.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's an important detail.

Now, could you tell me about your living situation with Alex? Is he living with you, or do you contribute to the cost of supporting him (for example, paying for his food or accommodation)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Just a couple more questions.

Are you responsible for Alex? In other words, are you the person who is mainly responsible for looking after him and making decisions about his care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, my ex-partner already claims Child Benefit for him, and Alex lives with both of us.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know – that's an important detail.

Under the Child Benefit rules, only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any one time. If your ex-partner is already receiving Child Benefit for Alex, you would not be able to make a separate claim for him while that claim is active.

However, if Alex lives with both of you but spends more time living with you, or if you become the person mainly responsible for him, you may be able to take over the claim. 

Could you clarify – does Alex spend more time living with you, or does he split his time equally between both homes?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with both of us in the same household - we all live together.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Ah, I see – thank you for clarifying that. So you, your ex-partner, and Alex all live together in the same household.

In this situation, only one person in the household can claim Child Benefit for Alex at any one time. Since your ex-partner is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you would not be able to make a separate claim while their claim is active.

If you and your ex-partner would like to change who receives the Child Benefit, your ex-partner would need to stop their claim, and then you could apply. However, you cannot both claim simultaneously for the same child.

Let me now provide you with my assessment based on everything you've told me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, here is my assessment:

---

**Child Benefit Eligibility for Alex: Not Eligible**

**Reasoning:**
- Alex is 19 years old and studying A-levels in sixth form, which counts as approved education.
- He started this course before turning 19, which is a requirement for continuing Child Benefit past age 16.
- However, your ex-partner is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex, and you all live together in the same household.
- **Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any one time.** Since your ex-partner already has an active claim, you cannot make a separate claim for Alex.

---

**What you can do:**
If you would like to become the person receiving Child Benefit for Alex, your ex-partner would need to end their current claim first. Once their claim has stopped, you could then apply, and Alex would still meet the eligibility criteria as long as he remains in approved education.

Is there anything else I can help you with?

However, the claimant's ex-partner is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex, and all three of them live together in the same household. Under Child Benefit rules, only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any given time. Since a claim is already active for Alex by the ex-partner, the claimant is not eligible to make a separate claim for Alex at this time.
arguments.overall_reasoning: The claimant is not currently eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex because another person (their ex-partner) is already claiming Child Benefit for him, and only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child at any one time. If the ex-partner were to stop their claim, the claimant could then apply to receive Child Benefit for Alex, provided he continues to meet the other eligibility criteria (remaining in approved education until at least 28 February following his 19th birthday).
